contract: The reviewed decisions that release a REVIEW-tier validation hold, and the only input that can (src/services/catalog.logic.ts::resolveCatalogDisposition takes no other, and takes nothing at all from the advisory second-model review). scripts/catalog-validate.ts loads this document, resolves the decisions that cover each row, and passes their check names to the checks as curatorAllowlistedCheckNames; every lift it applies is recorded as an assumption on that food's catalog_validation_records row naming the check, decidedBy, decidedOn and this version, so a published row states who released it. WHAT A DECISION MAY DO: name one review-tier check (out_of_category_range or allergens_unknown, the two names catalogCheckTier puts in that tier) and a scope it applies to, so a candidate held by that check alone may publish. WHAT IT MAY NOT DO: nothing else. It cannot lift a quarantine-tier or reject-tier check — a record that cannot be true as written is not a curator's call, and catalog-validate refuses this whole document at load if a decision names one. It changes no stored fact about a food: allergen_status stays exactly as imported or generated, nutrition_provenance stays ai_estimated, and publication therefore does not make an AI row eligible for recipe planning (which requires allergen_status 'known' AND source_backed nutrition, AAP 0.7.3) nor remove its "AI estimate" label in Add Food (AAP 0.1.4 i). It cannot lift the identity floor, the pending-classification floor or the identity-evidence floor, which are validation's own and move for nothing in this file. EVERY ENTRY IS ATTRIBUTABLE: check, scope, decidedBy, decidedOn (ISO date) and rationale are all mandatory, and catalog-validate refuses the document if one is missing or blank — a decision nobody can attribute is not a decision. SCOPES: a per-food decision carries sourceKeys and applies to exactly those catalog_foods.source_key values; a class decision carries identitySource and, optionally, categories, and applies to every row of that identity source in those coverage-plan categories (absent or empty categories means every category). Adding, narrowing or withdrawing a decision is a reviewed data change to this file. It takes effect on the next validation pass that judges the rows it covers: an unchanged canonical pass is a no-op by design (see RE-RUNNING A SUCCEEDED PASS in catalog-validate.ts), so a decision added after a succeeded pass is applied by a new import, generation or load, by a new coveragePlanVersion, or by catalog:validate --revalidate-quarantined, which reconsiders exactly the held rows.

decisions.rationale: An explicitly unknown allergen set is a gap in a food's METADATA, not a claim that the food is unsafe, and holding every generated row on it left AI-assisted gap filling with no route to publication at all: allergen_status is 'unknown' on every candidate catalog-generate-ai.ts writes, so without this decision no generated food could ever reach published and the per-category coverage the plan asks AI generation to fill could only ever come from USDA. Lifting it is safe because publication does not promote the metadata: the row keeps allergen_status 'unknown' and nutrition_provenance 'ai_estimated', so recipe planning still excludes it (an ingredient must be allergen_status 'known' and source_backed), Add Food still renders it with the "AI estimate" pill, and the failed check stays recorded on the validation record for anyone reading it. The shipped v1 release is the precedent for treating the flag as informational rather than disqualifying: 9,298 of its 9,422 published USDA rows carry exactly this failed check, published because the vendor is authoritative about the food while nobody has reviewed its allergen list. What this decision changes is who says so for a generated row — a named curator rather than the model that proposed it. It does NOT extend to out_of_category_range: that flag is about an AI-derived nutrition VALUE sitting outside its category's plausible band, nothing outside the model has spoken for the number, and confirming it would make the generator the source of the claim under review (AAP 0.1.2). Such a row stays quarantined until a curator decides on that food specifically.
